title: A narrative states each figure in the role its input holds, or as a quoted text holds it
assertion: Passes: days, pages, versions, releases, levels, years, counts, units and rows each with their words, in digits, with commas or in words; a quoted figure beside its own words, in the role its quote gives it; at least 100 hand-written forms not drawn from the drafting templates; each figure in the role of the noun after it or its nearest cue (“the $30.00 difference”, “the payer paid the contract rate”, a deadline after “days after payment”), “respectively” in order in its two plain forms, its cues right before the list (“The contract expected and the payer allowed $100.00 and $70.00, respectively”) or right after it (“$100.00 and $70.00 were the expected and allowed amounts per line, respectively”, “$100.00 and $70.00, respectively, were ...”), each figure in its cue’s scope (“$300.00 and $70.00 were expected in total and allowed per line, respectively”, or with each between commas), else the whole list’s (after “amounts”, or between the list and its cues), else the sentence’s opening scope phrase’s, never a clause after “respectively”; a sentence’s opening scope phrase (“For each line,”, “In total,”) for each figure whose own clause states none, never one whose clause states its own (“..., while across the 3 lines it allowed $210.00”, “..., and $210.00 for the claim”); one row named alone as a line (“the claim line”, “on line 1”, “Patient 2’s line”, “the third line”); an earlier clause’s figure beside a “respectively” list as its own (“The payer paid $56.00 per line, while $100.00 and $70.00 were the expected and allowed amounts per line, respectively”); an amount with no scope where its role’s per-line and total values are one; each line’s and the lines’ totals, ordinals and partitives as prose (“the first 3 claims”, “2 of the 3 claims”), “Lines 1–3”, a locked fee schedule’s year and business days to pay; a number with no role fails
noFileReason: Narratives against the SYNTHETIC packets of @tp/packets/testing (role-examples.ts): no file.
